answer.effective_date: Effective 11/15/2025; Last Review Date 04/21/2025 (Status: Revised). Note: 'Approval and implementation dates for specific health plans may vary,' so Anthem's actual adoption date for this Nevada member's plan year could not be independently confirmed beyond the fact that Anthem Nevada's precertification list currently routes musculoskeletal/joint-surgery codes, including shoulder surgery, to Carelon Medical Benefits Management, which publishes this guideline.
criteria_quotes: General framework (applies to all Carelon Joint Surgery guideline determinations): 'Prior to any intervention, it is essential that the clinician confirms the diagnosis or establishes its pretest likelihood based on a complete evaluation of the patient. This includes a history and physical examination and, where applicable, a review of relevant laboratory studies, diagnostic testing, and response to prior therapeutic intervention... Providers may be required to submit clinical documentation in support of a request for services. Such documentation must a) accurately reflect the clinical situation at the time of the requested service, and b) sufficiently document the ordering provider's clinical intent.'

Acute full-thickness tear: 'Rotator cuff repair is considered medically necessary for an acute full thickness tear when ALL the following criteria are met: Traumatic injury within the preceding 3 months with no preexisting shoulder pain (For traumatic injuries that occurred more than 3 months ago, see chronic or degenerative [tear criteria])...'

Chronic/degenerative full-thickness tear: 'Rotator cuff repair is considered medically necessary for a chronic or degenerative full thickness tear when ALL the following criteria are met: Gradual onset of shoulder pain in the absence of a significant traumatic event within the preceding 3 months; Pain ≥ 3 on the VAS scale which interferes with age-appropriate activities of daily living; Physical exam consistent with symptomatic rotator cuff tear (e.g., drop arm test, painful arc, full/empty can test, weakness of internal/external rotation or abduction); Recent advanced imaging confirms features of a degenerative full thickness tear; Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management.'
Partial-thickness tear: '...Recent advanced imaging confirms features of a partial thickness tear; Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management.'

Revision rotator cuff repair carries its own separate 'ALL the following criteria' list and an added tobacco-cessation requirement: 'adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco and nicotine products for at least 6 weeks prior to revision surgery is required.'

answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: Because the denial was based on 'incomplete documentation,' the patient's provider/patient should call the Anthem/Carelon precertification line (per Anthem's Nevada precertification list, Carelon Medical Benefits Management can be reached at 877-291-0366, or submissions can be made at https://www.providerportal.com) or call Anthem member services (number on the ID card) and explicitly request: (a) the specific Carelon 'Joint Surgery' guideline criteria applied to CPT 29827 for this member's plan, and (b) an itemized list of what documentation was missing from the request.
